title: Lavender inhalation for acute anxiety
subtitle: A steam inhalation of dried lavender flower for moments of acute anxiety and panic
excerpt: Lavender inhalation is a bowl of just-boiled water with a handful of dried lavender flowers, breathed slowly for 5 to 10 minutes. Traditionally prepared in the European home for moments of acute anxiety, panic, or the kind of wound-up feeling that won't release. The floral steam is immediate and direct. One session uses 2 tablespoons of dried flower; the rest of the jar keeps 12 months.

glossaryTerms.definition: A preparation where dried herb is added to a bowl of just-boiled water and the aromatic steam is breathed in slowly, under a towel, to deliver volatile plant compounds directly to the respiratory system and the olfactory nerve.

content.text: is a bowl of just-boiled water with 2 tablespoons of dried lavender flower. Breathed slowly for 5 to 10 minutes under a towel. For moments of acute anxiety, sharp panic, or mounting worry. The aromatic compounds reach the brain within seconds.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 2 tablespoons of dried lavender flower in a large heatproof bowl.
Pour 500 ml of just-boiled water over the flowers. The steam will rise immediately and carry the floral aromatic oils with it.

Drape a large towel over the back of your head and lean over the bowl so that the towel creates a tent over your head and the bowl. Keep your face 20 to 30 cm above the water, not directly at the surface.
Breathe slowly and steadily through the nose for 5 to 10 minutes. If the steam feels too hot, raise your head further from the bowl. Come out from under the towel for a breath of cool air if needed.
Use when needed during acute anxiety, up to once or twice a day. Not a daily long-term routine in the same way as an infusion. this is an on-the-moment preparation.
Dried lavender flower stores 12 months in a sealed tin kept away from light and heat. Prepare each session fresh.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use a steam inhalation if steam makes breathing uncomfortable, for example during an asthma flare. For severe panic disorder or anxiety that limits daily life, seek advice from a doctor or mental health professional.
